title: bug: publicationCredentialArguments hard-fails every remote git cannot url-match, so no scp-style SSH remote is publishable
description:
Filed by worker-bcaa6d5e from task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 (Gate 3 browser proof), 2026-09-08. That row is BLOCKED on this one.

THE DEFECT. apps/daemon/src/repository/git-publication-credentials.ts:7-8 runs `git config --null --get-urlmatch credential <remoteUrl>` and treats ONLY `code === 1 && stdout === ""` as "no credential configuration". Git answers exit **128** with `fatal: invalid URL scheme name or missing '://' suffix` for any remote that is not a scheme-bearing URL, so the next line throws PUBLISH_CREDENTIAL_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE and `createGitPublicationPort().push()` returns PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN having never attempted the push. `observe()` fails the same way with PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNREADABLE.

WHY IT IS A PRODUCTION BUG, not a test-lane one. `admitRemoteUrl` (publish-receipt-contracts.ts:77-85) DELIBERATELY admits scp-style SSH remotes through REMOTE_SSH -- `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` has no `://` and is the form `gh` and GitHub hand users by default. Every such remote is admitted by the ledger, stored, re-admitted on read, and then made UNPUSHABLE by this call. The publish silently reports PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN, which reads as a transport fault rather than "this daemon cannot use the remote you bound".

MEASURED, not inferred (probe run at HEAD 7e76c556, deleted after):
  GIT ["--git-dir=...\\.git","config","--null","--get-urlmatch","credential","C:/.../release-remote.git"] -> 128 "" "fatal: invalid URL scheme name or missing '://' suffix\n"
  PUSH   : {"ok":false,"code":"PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN","detail":"PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN"}
  OBSERVE: {"ok":false,"code":"PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNREADABLE","detail":"PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNREADABLE"}
With the SAME candidate and the credential read stubbed to `{code:1,stdout:""}` (i.e. "no credential config"), both succeed against real git:
  GIT [...,"push","--no-verify","--","C:/.../release-remote.git","7b45c4d5...:refs/heads/main"] -> 0
  PUSH   : {"ok":true}
  OBSERVE: {"ok":true,"sha":"7b45c4d54a2d281ebbb947d0475e07b3ba9be28b"}
So the credential read is the ONLY thing standing between the production port and a working push.

FIX DIRECTION (the implementer confirms it, this is not a mandate): treat "git cannot url-match this remote" as "there is no credential configuration for it" -- i.e. admit exit 128 with the invalid-URL-scheme fatal alongside the existing exit-1 case -- rather than as an unreadable configuration. Do NOT widen it to every nonzero exit: a genuinely unreadable config must still fail closed. Keep the injection-guard on values (`/[\r\n\0]/`) and the three-key allowlist exactly as they are.

WHY task-817d893f WAITS ON THIS. Its Playwright journey needs a PUSHED publication before the release card can offer a sha (release-evidence-read.ts:216). A hermetic lane cannot use a network remote, and a local bare repository -- a real git remote, real objects, real refs -- is admitted by `admitRemoteUrl` and then refused here. With this fixed, that journey is hermetic and green; without it, the only remaining path is pushing a branch to a real GitHub repository on every browser-suite run, which is an outward-facing side effect no test suite should carry.
definitionOfDone: `publicationCredentialArguments` returns [] (no credential arguments) for a remote git cannot url-match, and still THROWS PUBLISH_CREDENTIAL_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE for a genuinely unreadable configuration. Both arms asserted by their distinguishing condition, not merely by 'did not throw'.

A test pins the exact git behaviour this depends on: `git config --null --get-urlmatch credential <non-url>` exits 128 with `fatal: invalid URL scheme name or missing '://' suffix`. Assert the exit code AND the stderr line, so a future git that changes either is caught here rather than in a browser lane.
An arm proves the scp-style SSH remote `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` -- which `admitRemoteUrl` admits -- now reaches the push rather than refusing PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN at the credential read.

`createGitPublicationPort().push()` and `.observe()` both succeed end to end against a REAL local bare repository, asserting `{ok:true}` and `{ok:true, sha:<the approved sha>}` respectively. This is the arm task-817d893f's journey depends on.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: ONE FILE, ONE CONDITION. The fix is the acceptance predicate in git-publication-credentials.ts. Do not widen it to accept every nonzero exit, do not touch admitRemoteUrl's admission policy, and do not add a seam to inject the git port -- the lane keeps the publisher real on purpose.

FAIL CLOSED STAYS. A config read that genuinely cannot be parsed must still throw PUBLISH_CREDENTIAL_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE with the same code. Assert the refusing arm by its CODE, and confirm it goes red when the production predicate is mutated.

THE FIX — one condition, one file, one added production line.

apps/daemon/src/repository/git-publication-credentials.ts now reads (line numbers at this tree):
   5  /**
   6   * Git refuses to url-match a remote with no `://` scheme (scp-style SSH, a local bare repository).
   7   * `LC_ALL=C` is pinned by `landingEnvironment()`, so this line is stable; an unrecognised stderr still fails closed.
   8   */
   9  export const UNMATCHABLE_REMOTE_FATAL = "fatal: invalid URL scheme name or missing '://' suffix";
  ...
  18    if (result.code === 1 && result.stdout === "") return [];
  19    if (result.code === 128 && result.stdout === "" && result.stderr.split(/\r?\n/u).some((line) => line === UNMATCHABLE_REMOTE_FATAL)) return [];
  20    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error("PUBLISH_CREDENTIAL_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE");
(the constant landed in step 1 for the import-resolution reason recorded there; line 19 is this step's entire production change.)

Line-EQUALITY per split line, as specified — not `stderr.includes`, not a trimmed whole-buffer compare, not `code !== 0`. `\r?\n` handles Windows git's CRLF. A path or value echoed inside some other fatal cannot spoof the admission, and `code: null` (nodeGitRunner's timeout/spawn shape) is not `=== 128` so it still falls through to the throw.

BYTE-IDENTICAL, verified by reading the diff: the three-key allowlist (credential.helper / credential.usehttppath / credential.username), the `/[\r\n\0]/u` value injection guard, the missing-separator throw, and the `--get-urlmatch` argv. No change to admitRemoteUrl. No new key on GitPublicationOptions — the `readConfig` seam step 4 needs already exists at git-publication-port.ts:26/33 (`options.readConfig ?? options.run ?? nodeGitRunner`), so task rail 1's "do not add a seam" is satisfied by using what is there.

THE PORT ARMS, REAL GIT, NO NETWORK (DoD 3 and DoD 4). In git-publication-native.test.ts add two tests, reusing the existing file's temp-repo idiom (init, commit, capture via createPublicationCandidateReader, `git init --bare` remote, rmSync in finally under a startsWith guard):
  ARM A (DoD 4) — the candidate's approval.remoteUrl IS the real local bare repository path (verified admitted by admitRemoteUrl at plan time; createPublicationCandidateReader returns ok). Drive `createGitPublicationPort({})` with NO options at all, so both the push runner and the credential read are production defaults. Assert `await port.push(candidate)` toEqual({ ok: true }) and `await port.observe(candidate)` toEqual({ ok: true, sha: candidate.approval.sha }), and additionally that `git --git-dir=<remote> rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>` equals that sha. This is the arm task-817d893f's Playwright journey depends on; before step 2 it returns PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN / PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNREADABLE (measured at plan time on this exact shape).
  ARM B (DoD 3) — the candidate's approval.remoteUrl is the scp-style `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`. Pass `readConfig: nodeGitRunner` EXPLICITLY so the unswapped scp-style string reaches the real credential read, and `run: async (cwd, args) => publicationGitRunner(cwd, args.map((a) => a === candidate.approval.remoteUrl ? remote : a))` so the push lands in the local bare repository and NOTHING touches the network. Record the argv the run wrapper sees; assert push toEqual({ ok: true }) AND that a recorded argv contains "push" — i.e. the call reached the push instead of refusing PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN at the credential read. Omitting readConfig makes this arm silently test the local path instead of the scp-style remote; do not omit it.
Do not modify the existing test in this file.

DoD 3 and DoD 4 — two port arms in git-publication-native.test.ts, real git, real objects, real refs, no network. The existing test (lines 11-35) is UNTOUCHED; a shared `publishableFixture` helper was added below it rather than refactoring it.

ARM A (DoD 4), `pushes and observes a real local bare remote end to end with no injected options at all` (line 49):
  expect(admitRemoteUrl(remote)).toBe(remote);            // the ledger's own policy admits the local bare path — asserted, not assumed
  const port = createGitPublicationPort({});              // NO options: run = publicationGitRunner, configRunner = nodeGitRunner, both production defaults
  expect(await port.push(candidate)).toEqual({ ok: true });
  expect(await port.observe(candidate)).toEqual({ ok: true, sha: candidate.approval.sha });
  expect(git(`--git-dir=${remote}`, "rev-parse", "refs/heads/approved")).toBe(candidate.approval.sha);
The candidate's `approval.remoteUrl` IS the bare repository path, captured through the production `createPublicationCandidateReader(root)` (which itself refuses via admitRemoteUrl), so the whole chain is the production admission policy — nothing routes around it. This is the arm task-817d893f's Playwright journey depends on: it is exactly the shape that returned PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN / PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNREADABLE before step 2.

ARM B (DoD 3), `reaches the push for an scp-style ssh remote instead of refusing at the credential read` (line 64):
  expect(admitRemoteUrl(scpStyle)).toBe(scpStyle);              // "git@github.com:owner/repo.git"
  expect(candidate.approval.remoteUrl).toBe(scpStyle);          // the unswapped scp string is what the port holds
  createGitPublicationPort({ readConfig: nodeGitRunner, run: <recording wrapper> })
`readConfig: nodeGitRunner` is passed EXPLICITLY, as the step requires: without it, configRunner falls through to `options.run` and the credential read would see the REWRITTEN local path — the arm would silently test ARM A again. With it, the real credential read receives the scp-style string and hits the exit-128 path this row fixes.

CORRECTED ASSERTION, worth recording because the first version was wrong and green-looking is not the failure mode here. I first asserted `expect(argv.flat()).not.toContain(scpStyle)` against a single recorded list, and it went RED:
  AssertionError: expected [ 'init', '--bare', …(17) ] to not include 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git'
That red was correct and my assertion was backwards: the recorded list is the argv the PRODUCTION PORT BUILT, i.e. pre-swap, so of course it carries the scp remote — that is the very thing DoD 3 wants proven. The wrapper now records BOTH sides and asserts each for what it actually shows:
  const pushArgv = built.find((args) => args.includes("push"));
  expect(pushArgv).toBeDefined();
  expect(pushArgv).toContain(scpStyle);        // DoD 3: the port REACHED the push carrying the scp-style remote
  expect(spawned.flat()).not.toContain(scpStyle);  // and real git never received it — no run of this suite can reach github.com
Plus `git --git-dir=<remote> rev-parse refs/heads/approved` === the approved sha, so the push really moved objects into the bare repository rather than merely exiting 0.

The network-safety proof is now positive rather than assumed: `spawned` is every argv handed to publicationGitRunner, and no element of it equals the scp remote.
